articles.headline: Bitcoin jumps 26% after largest short squeeze s...
articles.description: Bitcoin surged 26% from its mid-August low following the largest single-day short liquidation event since 2019, with 85% of liquidated positions being shorts. During this period, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $2.23 billion in creations, indicating strong spot-market demand that supported the price rise despite a decline in leveraged futures positions. Futures open interest fell 11% in Bitcoin terms, showing the rally was not fueled by increased leverage. The market now watches if spot demand and futures leverage will grow together or if the rally will continue with subdued leverage.

articles.headline: Bitcoin ETFs see $21M inflow, easing recent sel...
articles.description: Bitcoin ETFs experienced a $21.13 million inflow on Friday, led by Blackrock’s IBIT, signaling a pause after two days of heavy redemptions totaling nearly $1 billion. This modest inflow suggests institutional selling pressure on Bitcoin may be easing, though it remains to be seen if this will lead to renewed buying. Meanwhile, Ether ETFs continued to face outflows, losing $56.10 million and extending their streak to nine consecutive days, highlighting a divergence in institutional interest between Bitcoin and Ether. NEAR ETFs attracted fresh capital, contrasting with outflows in Solana ETFs, reflecting selective investor preferences. Overall, Bitcoin's price stability depends on whether new institutional demand can pick up, as current gains are largely driven by existing holders rather than fresh inflows.
